Subject: Next steps: Bridge demo + SDK environment sanity kit

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so your eng/security teams have a clear on-ramp.

High-level scope we discussed:
- Use-case: in-product assistant for clinicians + fast patient summary (low latency, controlled hallucination)
- Integration surface: Redwood hosted API initially, with Dedicated reserved capacity for production.
- Tech areas to validate this week: SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript), auth pattern (API keys vs OIDC), request routing for regional failover, structured output / tool-calling for EHR lookup, and embeddings + reranker for semantic search.

Proposed immediate deliverables (what I'll send now):
1) bridge-demo-sample.tar.gz — minimal sample apps (py/ts) that run locally and call Redwood with an env var-based auth pattern.
2) redwood-sdk-smoke-checklist.pdf — a short checklist you can run with your devs to confirm environment parity.
3) auth-config-snippet.txt — example OIDC + API-key hybrid pattern and config notes for audit logs.

Next steps I suggest:
- Your eng team runs the smoke checklist and confirms local run (we aim for under 2 hours).
- If OIDC is required, security can review auth-config-snippet.txt and we’ll follow-up with a short tech call to align KMS/audit expectations.
- Schedule a 30-minute sandbox demo once you’ve run the smoke checklist — I recommend early next week.

Attach: bridge-demo-sample.tar.gz (sample apps), redwood-sdk-smoke-checklist.pdf, auth-config-snippet.txt

Thanks — happy to jump on a screenshare.

—

Sofia — really helpful summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we run the checklist: 

1) Auth: Our security team prefers OIDC for service-to-service tokens and needs assurance around audit logging/audit trail retention. Is the auth-config-snippet.txt showing a full flow with refresh token rotation + KMS integration?

2) Embeddings / Rerank: For our patient search we want deterministic reranking behavior. Do your sample apps include an end-to-end example: embed -> index -> rerank on top of generation?

3) Local infra: Our devs will run the samples on macOS dev boxes and a Linux CI runner. Any known Linux kernel / Docker engine caveats we should watch for?

We’ll try the run today — I’ll loop in Oliver for scheduling the sandbox demo.

Thanks,

Emily — great questions, answers below plus a tiny code/config snippet to help your security and infra teams triage quickly.

Auth & audit logging:
- The auth-config-snippet.txt contains an example OIDC exchange flow (client credentials) and the hybrid pattern we recommend when customers want short-lived API keys for CI but OIDC for services.
- Audit logs: Redwood Private and Dedicated both emit per-request audit logs (identity, model, route, token id) to customer-backed storage. We can show retention policy options (30 / 90 / 365 days) on the tech call.

Embeddings + rerank:
- bridge-demo includes a tiny pipeline:
  1) python samples/embeddings_index.py -> create embeddings, store to a local vector store (faiss).
  2) typescript samples/query_rerank.ts -> run retrieval, then pass topK+context to the model for generation and reranking using a small scoring function.
- The reranker is deterministic given the same candidate set and seed; we include an optional calibration step (score normalization) in the sample.

Local infra caveats:
- Docker: ensure your Linux CI runner has user namespaces enabled for the sample sandbox (--userns-remap) or run the non-container path in samples/local_run.sh. macOS uses the native binary build; no special kernel flags required.
- GPU: samples are CPU-first; if you test quantized local builds for speed, note that glibc 2.29+ is required.

Inline snippet (auth-config-snippet.txt is attached but here is the key part):

# OIDC client credentials flow (example)
CLIENT_ID=gw-client
CLIENT_SECRET=<<redacted>>
TOKEN_ENDPOINT=https://auth.greenwavehealth.com/oauth2/token
RENEWAL_WINDOW=60 # seconds before expiry to rotate

# Env var for Redwood SDK
REDWOOD_API_MODE=private
REDWOOD_AUDIT_LOG_URI=s3://gw-audit-logs/redwood/

If you want, Karthik and I can hop on a short call with your security team to walk through this.

Propose: I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute sandbox walkthrough — can you do Wed 8/1 10:00 AM PT?

—

Emily — jumping in to own the smoke test assistance. A couple operational notes and the quick checklist highlights so your devs can start with minimal friction: 

Quick smoke checklist (top items):
- Unpack: tar -xzf bridge-demo-sample.tar.gz && cd bridge-demo
- Python path: .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
- TS path: cd ts-sample && npm ci && npm run build
- Set env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY or OIDC vars per auth-config-snippet.txt
- Run local embedding indexing: python samples/embeddings_index.py --local-db faiss
- Run query + rerank: node samples/query_rerank.js --topk 5

Attachments: redwood-sdk-smoke-checklist.pdf contains a one-page verification table your devs can check off. If you hit any permission/audit log routing issues, ping me directly (marcus@redwood.com) and I’ll triage with infra.

I’ll create a shared ephemeral sandbox in our Dedicated test pool for the demo if you confirm Wed 8/1 10:00 AM PT — that will let us show latency numbers and routing fallback.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
